title: This World #1 Golf Coach Shows Me How to Easily Hit Your Driver & Irons Pure

people.coach: Chris; Chris Mayson Golf branding visible in the lesson
people.attribution_basis: Spoken first name and visible lesson signage; no claim based on facial identification.

context.clubs: Iron practice and driver/iron applications; specific clubs identified only where spoken.
context.golfer_report: Returning after an arm injury and time away; source includes joking dialogue, so no medical conclusions are drawn.
context.style: Technical diagnosis, physical guidance, exaggerated feels, repeated feedback, blunt conversational delivery. This delivery style is not automatically prescribed to app users.
context.body_screening: No formal body handicap or physical screen shown in the reviewed lesson.

coverage.transcript_kind: YouTube en-orig automatic captions; speaker changes inferred from dialogue/video, not diarization metadata.
coverage.visual_review_method: 61 overview frames across the full timeline; 100 targeted detail frames, 48 sequence frames, and 12 preset-rehearsal frames, all 20 contact sheets inspected. Repeated timestamps may occur across sets. This is sampled visual review, not continuous playback.
limitations: At 480p, replay panels and tablets are small; exact grip/face/angle values cannot be measured reliably.
No legible monitor metric table or force/pressure plot verified.
Caption timing is source playback time, not real swing time.
The edited video interleaves earlier lessons and course inserts; timestamps are not a single chronological practice session.

cases.title: Inside takeaway and excessive arm depth: rebuild width before adding downswing changes
cases.coaching_finding: Chris identifies an inside/closed first move and excessive rotation/arm depth in Jerome's backswing.
cases.coach_reasoning: He links the backswing to the unwanted rightward delivery and closed face, while judging the golfer's existing lead-side movement adequate.

intervention.intended_change: Keep arm structure wider and less wrapped behind the torso, with an improved takeaway and top position.
feel: Take the club outward relative to Jerome's habitual inward move.
Keep hand width while winding to the top; stop arms with the turn.
drill: Pause at shaft-horizontal P2.
Turn slowly to the top while maintaining width.
Hit a soft shot, then join the stages as the shape becomes repeatable.
avoid_literal_interpretation: Do not freeze the hips or remove the turn.
Do not prescribe an objectively wide-open clubface because the feel seems open.
Do not turn a slow-drill pressure sensation into a normal-swing pressure target.

applicability: Right-handed example with pushes/hooks and coach-confirmed inside takeaway plus excessive depth/rotation.
Check camera view, intended shot shape, clubface context, and more than one swing before applying to another golfer.
unknowns: No validated arm-width or face-angle threshold.
No measured mobility screening.
Captioned path values lack legible instrument confirmation.
cases.observed_result: Coach reports improved position and several less-inside paths, but later values fluctuate. Edited course examples show application without a controlled retention test.

selection.reassess: Verify takeaway/top on video, then inspect strike and ball flight before adding a delivery change.

cases.title: Repeatable setup with a driver exception
cases.coaching_finding: Chris repeatedly corrects Jerome's setup process.
cases.coach_reasoning: He uses a consistent order to make ball position and balance repeatable as stance width changes.

drill: Grip and place feet together.
Rest club on the ground and set posture.
Use the demonstrated lead-foot placement, then trail-foot placement to set stance width.
For driver, use the stated lead-heel exception.
feel: Notice whether balance feels toward toes or heels.

applicability: Treat as this coach's setup routine and calibrate for club/golfer.
Requires a view that reveals feet, ball, and posture.
unknowns: Four-inch rule is not validated for every body, club, lie or shot.
Actual foot pressure cannot be recovered from these frames.
cases.observed_result: Coach approves later setups; no isolated setup-versus-control test.

selection.reassess: Check repeated address positions before changing swing mechanics.

cases.title: Reversed-hand rehearsal for a deep/across-line backswing
cases.coaching_finding: The same excessive-depth/across-line pattern needs a simpler physical feel.
cases.coach_reasoning: Chris says the changed hand order encourages trail-arm folding while keeping the lead arm wide and the trail arm in front.

drill: For the demonstrated right-handed golfer, put the left hand below the right.
Rehearse the backswing with trail arm folding and lead arm extending.
Return to normal grip and reproduce the arm-structure feel.
feel: Lead arm over trail arm; width at the top.
intervention.delivery_mode: Rehearsal then normal-grip transfer; no full-speed reversed-grip hitting prescription.

applicability: Use as an alternative way to teach the C01 pattern when verbal instruction is hard to execute.
Match handedness explicitly; left-handed adaptation was not demonstrated.
unknowns: No dose/repetition count or measured isolated outcome.
No physical-screen prerequisites supplied.
cases.observed_result: Jerome rehearses the change and coach guides it; transfer is demonstrated, sustained performance untested.

selection.reassess: Normal-grip video should retain the intended structure without creating another compensation.

cases.title: Shoulder, turn, extend rehearsal to locate an individual top position
cases.coaching_finding: Jerome needs a repeatable way to find the wider top position rather than guess or wrap arms around himself.
cases.coach_reasoning: Chris uses a staged physical rehearsal and then adjusts the hands to help Jerome recognise that position.

drill: Take normal grip and place the club on the shoulder.
Adopt posture, turn, then push arms away.
Inspect and adjust with the coach.
Return to address and recreate the position in a backswing.
feel: Arms remain in front with width; the body still turns.

applicability: Alternative for the C01 arm-structure finding.
The resulting position must be checked for this golfer rather than assumed ideal.
unknowns: No universal angles, rep count or independent striking test.
The source does not assess physical capacity for another golfer.
cases.observed_result: Jerome reproduces the rehearsal and says it matches the previous feel; coach makes a small adjustment.

selection.reassess: Compare rehearsed position with an ordinary backswing and check that the turn remains.

cases.title: Release advice must match grip and wrist structure
cases.coaching_finding: Jerome worries he holds the club stable too long and asks for release timing.
cases.coach_reasoning: Chris considers grip and wrist flexion before discussing release, and judges a new timing thought unnecessary for this golfer.

intervention.action: Keep the existing priority on backswing structure; do not add conscious release timing in this case.
intervention.educational_content: Different grip/wrist combinations can call for different release patterns in the coach's framework.
intervention.withheld_instruction: No universal release instant or tour-player copying prescription.

applicability: Requires confirmed grip/wrist/face context and actual ball-flight/strike problem.
Educational explanation can answer a question without creating another active swing task.
unknowns: No precise 3D wrist, face or sequence measurements.
Tour-player examples and force language need independent review before becoming general rules.
cases.observed_result: No controlled release intervention is performed; this is evidence for withholding an unnecessary change.

selection.reassess: Revisit only if verified residual delivery/face evidence remains.

cases.title: Troubleshoot residual curvature after checking the original change
cases.coaching_finding: Ball flight improves but some shots remain too far inside or curve more than intended.
cases.coach_reasoning: Chris checks the original backswing change before changing the downswing; later he explicitly permits a delivery adjustment only when width, alignment and face are satisfactory.

decision_steps: Check intended start line and curvature against the actual shot.
Check takeaway/top against the agreed source-specific finding.
If the original change is absent, continue that intervention.
If the backswing meets the agreed checks and unwanted draw remains, consider the cut/leftward delivery feel.
feel: A cut feel is a conditional next step, not a mandatory simultaneous third thought.

applicability: This decision procedure follows a previously assessed pushes/hooks case.
Needs reliable ball-flight evidence and view-appropriate swing evidence.
unknowns: No measured universal definition of satisfactory top/face position.
Ball flight alone does not identify all causes, including strike location.
No automated recognition threshold established.
cases.observed_result: Coach supplies repeated correction and conditional escalation; reported path values vary rather than improve monotonically.

selection.reassess: Use later video and ball flight, not subjective unfamiliarity alone.

cases.title: Target-led pre-shot routine and useful post-shot review
cases.coaching_finding: Chris wants Jerome to prepare an intended shot and avoid running a mechanical checklist over the ball.
cases.coach_reasoning: He separates deciding, visualising and rehearsing from execution, then treats the outcome as confidence or information.

routine: Visualise the intended shot; the demonstrated breathing pattern is 4-in, 1-hold, 4-out.
Reinforce a successful feel or identify what to learn.
intervention.note: These are sequential routine stages, not five simultaneous swing thoughts.

applicability: Can support transferring a current coaching focus into play.
Target and distance rehearsal should be personalised.
unknowns: No isolated proof that the breathing cadence or routine improves score.
The 105-yard example is not another golfer's distance map.
cases.observed_result: Coach demonstrates the routine; the edited course footage is application evidence only.

selection.reassess: Record whether the golfer completed the routine and the intended-versus-actual shot.

cases.title: Clock-length wedge rehearsal requires individual calibration
cases.coaching_finding: Jerome needs an approximately 85-yard approach to a specific tier of a green.
cases.coach_reasoning: He describes choosing a familiar backswing length rather than adding hand manipulation to manufacture distance.

drill: Use personally calibrated clock-length rehearsals for the chosen wedge.
Select a landing area appropriate to the green and conditions.
intervention.attribution: Jerome's application; Chris separately demonstrates a different personal distance example.

applicability: Partial wedge shots with a golfer-specific calibration history.
unknowns: No validated clock-to-yardage table.
Lie, spin, wind and rollout are not controlled.
cases.observed_result: Jerome reports roughly 15 feet remaining and par; an edited example, not calibration evidence.

selection.reassess: Build a measured personal carry/dispersion record rather than copy this yardage.

cases.coach_reasoning: Chris contrasts that with a pressure/stretch rehearsal, then in the present lesson says Jerome already performs that part well.

drill: In the earlier demonstration, keep the upper structure raised while rehearsing the move toward the lead foot.
Then allow the turn to follow.
intervention.current_case_action: Do not add this drill to Jerome's current backswing assignment.

applicability: Only consider after observing the relevant transition issue; current case explicitly withholds it.
Force/pressure claims require more than a phone image.
unknowns: No force-plate measurements, validated movement timing, dosage or screening.
Not evidence for a universal back-to-target or lead-foot force prescription.

cases.title: Set the club in front before turning: another rehearsal for width
cases.coaching_finding: An earlier lesson identifies arm lifting/late hinging while seeking a wider, flowing turn.
cases.coach_reasoning: Chris uses a preset structure to help Jerome feel a turn with width, rather than throwing arms behind or adding excessive rotation.

drill: Set the club in front as demonstrated.
Turn to the top retaining the arm structure.
Transfer the feeling to a normal backswing.

applicability: Alternative teaching route within the same width/arm-structure family.
Brief prior-session example should be used with its surrounding width explanation.
unknowns: Exact preset geometry and rep count not specified.
No separate measured result.
cases.observed_result: Coach demonstrates and golfer rehearses in the embedded clip.

selection.reassess: Normal-swing video must show the intended width while retaining turn.

cases.title: Choose a shot shape using the golfer's tendencies and available distance
cases.coaching_finding: Jerome has unwanted push/hook tendencies and sufficient distance in the coach's assessment.
cases.coach_reasoning: Chris is open to draw or fade but suggests exploring a fade for this player's pattern and speed.

intervention.action: Test a fade intention after the underlying backswing work and compare useful shot patterns.
feel: The source golfer uses a pull-cut intention.

applicability: Needs the player's chosen target, actual dispersion, distance needs and strike evidence.

unknowns: No measured speed/dispersion baseline or comparison over multiple rounds.
cases.observed_result: Jerome reports favourable positions on two edited holes; retention and comparative advantage remain unproven.
